# Spark Control Center 1.5.1

Cross-tenant storage grant management and clearer, transactional user-management audits.

## Storage permissions

- Administrators can select active users across tenants, with tenant names and storage-access status shown in the selector. Accounts in tenants with storage disabled remain visible but cannot receive new grants.
- Resolve each grant against the recipient's real tenant; never use a caller-supplied tenant or the administrator's tenant. Refresh the user list when reopening the grant dialog or using Refresh connections in Prefix permissions, without waiting for the bootstrap reconciliation loop.
- Keep delegated bucket/prefix/actions within the administrator's own grants. Recheck both accounts, tenant policies and existing grants inside the write transaction to prevent stale or overly broad delegation.
- Preserve user/tenant/prefix enforcement for data access. Moving an account does not transfer old grants into its new tenant. Administrators may revoke obsolete grants after a tenant move or account disablement.
- Apply the same management rules to S3/MinIO and GCS, and clarify the English and Chinese permission-page guidance. Bootstrap grants remain one-time grants; revocations survive Pod replacement.

## User-management audits

- Replace generic configuration entries for user changes with `USER_CREATE`, `USER_UPDATE`, `USER_DELETE` and `USER_TENANT_CHANGE`.
- Display the target username as the resource. Tenant changes include the target user ID and the previous/new tenant names and IDs; role, account-status and namespace changes are also described.
- Commit the audit and user change together in PostgreSQL. A failed audit rolls back the user mutation. Password changes are identified without recording passwords, hashes or tokens.

## Upgrade

Back up PostgreSQL and upgrade the frontend, backend and optional storage-plugin images together to `1.5.1`. No new grant migration is required. Review recipient tenant assignments and enable object storage for the desired tenant before granting access. Existing per-tenant grants are preserved, not widened automatically.

Release assets: `spark-control-center-1.5.1.tar`, `spark-control-center-backend-1.5.1.tar`, `spark-control-center-object-storage-1.5.1.tar` and `spark-control-center-1.5.1.tgz`. Images have no private registry prefix. No checksum file is generated.

Validation includes frontend tests/build, Go test/vet, PostgreSQL transaction/authorization regression, real MinIO integration, three-image recovery and workflow checks, Helm 3/4 validation and English desktop browser checks. GCS protocol tests use fixtures; real WIF/IAM acceptance remains deployment-specific.
